pages.text: Sunlight came through the little window opening. Quacks rose from the paddy below. Mom, who worked several paddies on her own, shook Dingding gently. "The ducks are out. Time to get up." Dingding pulled the blanket over their head. "I'll get up when the quacking stops..."
Mom tugged the blanket, but Dingding curled up and stayed still. "Why do ducks get up so early?" Mom took the water jug down to the paddy. Dingding went back to sleep.
Much later, Dingding opened their eyes. Oh! The sun was right in the middle of the window opening. Today, Dingding had promised to plant young rice with Mom. "Already?" Dingding stamped their feet.
Dingding went to the doorway. Mr. Ming, who kept ducks in the lowest paddy, was coming up the bank. "Just woke up? Shall we learn how to get up from my ducks?" He pointed down.
The ducks spread their wings and shook off the water. "When ducks wake up, they quack and stretch their wings." Mr. Ming stretched his hands up like wings. Dingding stretched both hands up, too.

Dingding stretched their arms high overhead and their legs all the way down. Their whole body grew long. Sleepiness seemed to slip out through their toes. "I'm wide awake! Ducks Go Quack, Dingding Stretches!" Dingding's eyes shone.

"After stretching, say good morning to the paddy," Mr. Ming whispered. Dingding opened their arms wide toward the lower paddy. "Hello, paddy! Ducks Go Quack, Dingding Stretches!" The ducks quacked back.

Last came washing! Dingding scooped cold water from the basin onto their cheeks. Water slipped between their fingers, and their cheeks grew smooth and clean. Dingding sniffed the fresh morning paddy air. "I got up by myself!"

Now Dingding knew the morning steps. "One, open my eyes when the ducks quack! Two, stretch! Three, wash with cold water!" The next day, Dingding got up before Mom could shake them. "Ducks Go Quack, Dingding Stretches!"

Mom hugged Dingding. "You got up with the ducks! Let's plant young rice." A morning stretch sent sleepiness far away. Dingding picked up the water jug and called, "Ducks Go Quack, Dingding Stretches!"
